prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one precise pixel-art visual target for Tequila Kill, a top-down western action game. A SMALL SALOON CORNER WITH PONCHO, redrawn from scratch for an authentic 16-bit pixel-art look, closer in rendering grammar to Zelda A Link to the Past.
Input image 1 is a CONTENT AND CHARACTER reference from the current game, not an edit target. Retain the identity of Poncho and recognizable saloon objects, but replace its overly fine illustrated texture. Input image 2 is a STYLE reference only: use its simple readable shapes and sparse color clusters; DO NOT reproduce its blur, JPEG artifacts, green setting, Link character, HUD, or Nintendo objects.

Produce a single finished game-screen study, landscape 4:3, filling the whole image. DESIGN IT AS A 256 x 192 PIXEL SCENE enlarged EXACTLY FOUR TIMES with nearest-neighbor to 1024 x 768. Deliberate hard square pixel clusters on a uniform grid throughout; staircase diagonals; absolutely NO antialiasing, blur, smoothing, gradients, painterly brushwork, high-resolution tiny details, depth of field, CRT or screenshot damage. This must look like artwork actually authored at native low resolution, not a detailed painting with a pixelation filter applied.

Camera: classic Zelda-style overhead room projection, floor seen from above, small frontal faces on the back wall and furniture. Orthogonal horizontal and vertical axes, NEVER isometric or a cinematic angled room. Only a compact section of the saloon, framed close enough that Poncho and furniture read immediately. A quiet blue-gray tiled floor with large clean untextured tile interiors, warm cream plaster back wall and simple dark wood trim. Short L-shaped wooden bar in the upper part, shelf with a few green/amber bottle silhouettes on the wall, one card table and two chairs off to one side, one clay pot and one barrel. Table with just two readable cream playing-card shapes and a small red chip cluster. A small brick-red rug with simple ochre motifs at the threshold. Preserve open navigable floor between the character and objects. Use the objects already present in the game, do not invent extra characters or action.

Poncho: the ONLY character, central open floor, clearly distinguishable from furniture. At the conceptual native resolution the full silhouette is approximately 24 pixels wide by 30 pixels high, not a tiny icon. Preserve his recognizable extremely broad straw-gold oval sombrero with a raised rounded olive crown, dark hat underside, a long brown triangular poncho with a simple stepped fringed hem falling almost to the ground and covering the feet, small partly hidden hand with a short revolver pointing right. Body stays upright; camera looks down onto the broad hat but also sees the draping fabric below. Do not turn him into Link or an ordinary cowboy in trousers. Make the hat readable with two broad gold shades and one highlight cluster; no straw hatching. Poncho has two broad brown fabric tones and a few bold ochre fringe pixels; no embroidery, no smooth drapery. Small hard-edged dark oval contact shadow anchors him to the floor.

Color and graphic grammar: restrained unified approximately 32-color scene palette; every material defined by 2 or 3 discrete flat tones. Warm amber wood, pale cream plaster, muted desaturated blue-gray floor, olive crown and gold hat, brick-red rug. Deep plum-brown outlines selectively around interactable objects and character; floor much quieter and lower contrast than Poncho and props. Shadows are compact hard-edged flat shapes consistent with top-left light, no transparency effects or lighting bloom. Confident clear silhouettes, large deliberate color clusters, readable charming sprite construction, very sparse texture. Make every pixel contribute to form. Enough material contrast to recognize the breakable pot, bottles and barrel, without outlines, icons, labels or extra markers.

No HUD, no text, no J1, no gauges, no grid overlay, no colored circle, no comparison panels, no frame or black margins. This is a new art-direction mockup, not an engine capture.
